thesis: Reported liquidity reduces immediate funding concern but does not establish commercial deployment economics at the valuation. The bear wins on execution and cash returns, not an unsupported insolvency claim.
strongest_counterexample: Reported $1.9bn liquidity and progressing commercial discussions materially improve the ability to pursue deployment.
invalidation_conditions: Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if a binding customer contract reaches financial close with all disclosed conditions precedent satisfied.
Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow.
evidence_gaps: Liquidity restrictions, binding customer economics and prospective project funding.
Underlying statement periods and forward-estimate dates are not fully supplied.
decisive_factors: Trailing P/E unavailable because the snapshot is loss-making; negative forward P/E denotes expected losses, not cheapness
Reported liquidity supports runway and commercial work has progressed
Reported liquidity materially improves the runway argument and should not be ignored
